claim: Breathing is a vital rhythmic behavior generated by hindbrain neuronal circuitry, including the preBötzinger complex network (preBötC) that controls inspiration.
source: Breathing is a vital rhythmic behavior generated by hindbrain neuronal circuitry, including the preBötzinger complex network (preBötC) that controls inspiration.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about respiratory control, supported by the broader literature context.

claim: The emergence of preBötC network activity during prenatal development has been described.
source: The emergence of preBötC network activity during prenatal development has been described, but little is known regarding inspiratory neurons expressing pacemaker properties at embryonic stages.
evidence: This statement references prior research findings without specific citations in this sentence.

claim: Little is known regarding inspiratory neurons expressing pacemaker properties at embryonic stages.
source: The emergence of preBötC network activity during prenatal development has been described, but little is known regarding inspiratory neurons expressing pacemaker properties at embryonic stages.
evidence: This identifies a knowledge gap in the literature that motivates the current study.

claim: Embryonic preBötC neurons exhibit heterogeneous pacemaker oscillatory properties relying on distinct combinations of burst-generating INaP and ICAN conductances.
source: Here, we combined calcium imaging and electrophysiological recordings in mouse embryo brainstem slices together with computational modeling to reveal the existence of heterogeneous pacemaker oscillatory properties relying on distinct combinations of burst-generating INaP and ICAN conductances.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the study's experimental data combining multiple methodologies.

claim: The respective proportion of the different inspiratory pacemaker subtypes changes during prenatal development.
source: The respective proportion of the different inspiratory pacemaker subtypes changes during prenatal development.
evidence: This is a primary finding from developmental comparisons in the study.

claim: Network rhythmogenesis switches from a purely INaP/ICAN-dependent mechanism at E16.5 to a combined pacemaker/network-driven process at E18.5.
source: Concomitantly, network rhythmogenesis switches from a purely INaP/ICAN-dependent mechanism at E16.5 to a combined pacemaker/network-driven process at E18.5.
evidence: This is a primary finding from pharmacological experiments at different developmental stages.

claim: Network rhythmogenesis undergoes important changes during prenatal development through alterations in both circuit properties and the biophysical characteristics of pacemaker neurons.
source: Our results provide the first description of pacemaker bursting properties in embryonic preBötC neurons and indicate that network rhythmogenesis undergoes important changes during prenatal development through alterations in both circuit properties and the biophysical characteristics of pacemaker neurons.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the combined experimental findings of the study.

claim: Rhythmogenesis relies on an interplay between intrinsic neuronal membrane properties and intercellular synaptic connectivity.
source: Considerable data accumulated over the last decades from both invertebrate and vertebrate models have established the general mechanistic principle that rhythmogenesis relies on an interplay between intrinsic neuronal membrane properties and intercellular synaptic connectivity.
evidence: This is established knowledge from the broader CPG literature.

claim: Two main processes underlie motor rhythm generation: (i) the CPG network contains endogenously oscillatory neurons (pacemakers) which drive the wider circuit, and/or (ii) the rhythm emerges from the pattern of synaptic connections within the network.
source: Two main processes that may operate in varying combinations underlie motor rhythm generation: (i) the CPG network in question contains endogenously oscillatory neurons, so-called pacemakers, which drive the wider circuit cell population, and/or (ii), the rhythm emerges from the pattern of synaptic connections within the network.
evidence: This is established knowledge about CPG mechanisms from the literature.

claim: Respiratory movements are driven by rhythmic motor activity generated by neuronal circuits located in the brainstem.
source: Respiratory movements are driven by rhythmic motor activity generated by neuronal circuits located in the brainstem.
evidence: This is established knowledge about respiratory control.

claim: The respiratory rhythm generator is composed of two interacting CPG circuits distributed bilaterally in the ventral part of the medulla.
source: The respiratory rhythm generator is composed of two interacting CPG circuits distributed bilaterally in the ventral part of the medulla.
evidence: This is established knowledge about respiratory circuit organization.

claim: The parafacial respiratory group (RTN/pFRG) appears to generate preinspiratory activity in neonates in vitro.
source: The first is the parafacial respiratory group (RTN/pFRG; Onimaru and Homma, 2003) that appears to generate preinspiratory activity in neonates in vitro, active expiration in adults and plays a prominent role in central chemosensitivity (Guyenet and Bayliss, 2015).
evidence: This is supported by cited references to prior research.

claim: The parafacial respiratory group plays a prominent role in central chemosensitivity.
source: The first is the parafacial respiratory group (RTN/pFRG; Onimaru and Homma, 2003) that appears to generate preinspiratory activity in neonates in vitro, active expiration in adults and plays a prominent role in central chemosensitivity (Guyenet and Bayliss, 2015).
evidence: This is supported by the cited reference (Guyenet and Bayliss, 2015).

claim: The preBötzinger complex has been established to be both sufficient and necessary for generating the inspiratory phase of respiration.
source: The second network is the preBötzinger complex (preBötC; Smith et al., 1991) which has now been established to be both sufficient and necessary for generating the inspiratory phase of respiration (Smith et al., 1991; Gray et al., 2001; McKay et al., 2005; Tan et al., 2008; Bouvier et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by multiple cited references.

claim: The excitatory glutamatergic preBötC network contains ~800 neurons.
source: The excitatory glutamatergic preBötC network contains ~800 neurons, some of which (≤15%) in neonatal mouse exhibit intrinsic pacemaker properties (Koshiya and Smith, 1999; Thoby-Brisson and Ramirez, 2001; Pena et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by cited references about preBötC network composition.

claim: Some preBötC neurons (≤15%) in neonatal mouse exhibit intrinsic pacemaker properties.
source: The excitatory glutamatergic preBötC network contains ~800 neurons, some of which (≤15%) in neonatal mouse exhibit intrinsic pacemaker properties (Koshiya and Smith, 1999; Thoby-Brisson and Ramirez, 2001; Pena et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by multiple cited references.

claim: The 'group pacemaker hypothesis' proposes that the rodent postnatal respiratory rhythm derives from an interaction between membrane properties (including pacemaker cellular properties) and synaptic coupling.
source: To date, a leading hypothesis, inscribed in the 'group pacemaker hypothesis', proposes that the rodent postnatal respiratory rhythm derives from an interaction between membrane properties (including pacemaker cellular properties) and synaptic coupling (Rekling and Feldman, 1998; Feldman and Del Negro, 2006; Feldman et al., 2013).
evidence: This is a hypothesis from the literature supported by cited references.

claim: The preBötzinger complex becomes functional during the last third of gestation in rodents.
source: It has been shown in rodents that the preBötzinger complex becomes functional during the last third of gestation (Pagliardini et al., 2003; Thoby-Brisson et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by cited references.

claim: At early embryonic stages, glutamatergic synaptic signaling is required for preBötC network output.
source: Already at early embryonic stages, glutamatergic synaptic signaling is required for preBötC network output (Thoby-Brisson et al., 2005; Wallen-Mackenzie et al., 2006), although the presence of embryonic inspiratory neurons endowed with intrinsic bursting properties has only been inferred (Thoby-Brisson et al., 2005; Bouvier et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by cited references.

claim: The presence of embryonic inspiratory neurons endowed with intrinsic bursting properties has only been inferred.
source: Already at early embryonic stages, glutamatergic synaptic signaling is required for preBötC network output (Thoby-Brisson et al., 2005; Wallen-Mackenzie et al., 2006), although the presence of embryonic inspiratory neurons endowed with intrinsic bursting properties has only been inferred (Thoby-Brisson et al., 2005; Bouvier et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by cited references and identifies a gap in direct evidence.

claim: Of the 84 pacemaker neurons identified in 69 embryo slice preparations, three distinct types of discharge pattern were observed.
source: Of the 84 pacemaker neurons identified in 69 embryo slice preparations, three distinct types of discharge pattern were observed that differed in the characteristics of the spontaneous depolarizing waveforms - or drive potentials (DPs) – that underlie their intrinsic bursting activities.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the experimental data.

claim: In the first group (n = 23), cells expressed long-lasting plateau-like DPs with action potentials occurring at the beginning of the plateau followed by a depolarization block.
source: In a first group (n = 23), the cells expressed long-lasting plateau-like DPs with action potentials occurring at the beginning of the plateau followed by a depolarization block during which the neuron remained at a depolarized membrane potential without further spike generation prior to a spontaneous return to resting potential (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is a primary finding from patch-clamp recordings shown in Figure 2A.

claim: The mean amplitude of square-wave DPs was 30.5 ± 6.6 mV (343 burst cycles measured from 12 neurons).
source: The mean amplitude of such square-wave DPs was 30.5 ± 6.6 mV (343 burst cycles measured from 12 neurons; Figure 2D1, left) and their mean duration was 2.9 ± 0.1s (Figure 2D1, right).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from experimental data shown in Figure 2D1.

claim: The mean duration of square-wave DPs was 2.9 ± 0.1s.
source: The mean amplitude of such square-wave DPs was 30.5 ± 6.6 mV (343 burst cycles measured from 12 neurons; Figure 2D1, left) and their mean duration was 2.9 ± 0.1s (Figure 2D1, right).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from experimental data shown in Figure 2D1.

claim: The mean membrane potential of plateau-like pacemaker neurons measured between their DPs was −52.7 ± 0.7 mV.
source: The mean membrane potential of these neurons measured between their DPs was −52.7 ± 0.7 mV.
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from experimental data.

claim: In the second group (n = 45), pacemaker neurons generated short-lasting oscillatory DPs with depolarizing amplitude and duration means of 12.8 ± 3.8 mV and 0.79 ± 0.01 s, respectively (1296 bursts measured from 23 neurons).
source: In a second group (n = 45), the pacemaker neurons generated short-lasting oscillatory DPs and associated bursts with depolarizing amplitude and duration means of 12.8 ± 3.8 mV and 0.79 ± 0.01 s, respectively (1296 bursts measured from 23 neurons; Figure 2B, D2).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from experimental data shown in Figure 2B and D2.

claim: The mean membrane potential between bursts for oscillatory pacemakers was −49.2 ± 0.5 mV.
source: Their mean membrane potential between bursts was −49.2 ± 0.5 mV.
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from experimental data.

claim: In the third group (n = 16), cells expressed a mixture of long- and short-lasting DPs with amplitude and duration means of 14.5 ± 7.5 mV and 1.74 ± 0.08 s, respectively (739 bursts measured from 15 neurons).
source: In the third group (n = 16), cells expressed a mixture of long- and short-lasting DPs, which overall had amplitude and duration means of 14.5 ± 7.5 mV and 1.74 ± 0.08 s, respectively (739 bursts measured from 15 neurons; Figure 2C, D3).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from experimental data shown in Figure 2C and D3.

claim: The mean inter-burst membrane potential of the mixed phenotype was −49.1 ± 0.7 mV.
source: The mean inter-burst membrane potential of the mixed phenotype was −49.1 ± 0.7 mV.
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from experimental data.

claim: The durations of the drive potentials were statistically different between the three groups (Mann-Whitney test, p<0.001).
source: The durations of the drive potentials were statistically different between the three groups (Mann-Whitney test, p<0.001; Figure 2D4, right), while the mean DP amplitude of plateauing pacemakers was significantly larger compared to the amplitudes of two other types (p< 0.001), which themselves were not significantly different (Figure 2D4, left).
evidence: This is a statistical analysis of experimental data shown in Figure 2D4.

claim: The mean DP amplitude of plateauing pacemakers was significantly larger compared to the amplitudes of two other types (p< 0.001).
source: The durations of the drive potentials were statistically different between the three groups (Mann-Whitney test, p<0.001; Figure 2D4, right), while the mean DP amplitude of plateauing pacemakers was significantly larger compared to the amplitudes of two other types (p< 0.001), which themselves were not significantly different (Figure 2D4, left).
evidence: This is a statistical analysis of experimental data shown in Figure 2D4.

claim: The mean resting membrane potential values were statistically different between both plateauing and oscillatory neurons (t-test, p<0.001).
source: Finally, the mean resting membrane potential values were statistically different between both plateauing and oscillatory neurons (t-test, p<0.001) and between plateauing and mixed pacemaker cells (t-test, p<0.002).
evidence: This is a statistical analysis of experimental data.

claim: The mean resting membrane potential values were statistically different between plateauing and mixed pacemaker cells (t-test, p<0.002).
source: Finally, the mean resting membrane potential values were statistically different between both plateauing and oscillatory neurons (t-test, p<0.001) and between plateauing and mixed pacemaker cells (t-test, p<0.002).
evidence: This is a statistical analysis of experimental data.

claim: The respiratory network at embryonic stages between E16.5 and E18.5 contains a subpopulation of pacemaker neurons endowed with heterogeneous burst-generating intrinsic properties.
source: Thus, together these data show that the respiratory network at embryonic stages between E16.5 and E18.5 already contains a subpopulation of pacemaker neurons and that these cells are endowed with heterogeneous burst-generating intrinsic properties.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data presented.

claim: I-V curves obtained from isolated plateauing (n = 6) and oscillatory (n = 14) pacemaker neurons expressed a non-linear deviation at hyperpolarized membrane potentials, indicating the activation of voltage-dependent membrane conductances.
source: I-V curves obtained from isolated plateauing (n = 6) and oscillatory (n = 14) pacemaker neurons expressed a non-linear deviation at hyperpolarized membrane potentials, indicating the activation of voltage-dependent membrane conductances (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is a finding from experimental data shown in Figure 3A with interpretation.

claim: Membrane potential depolarization with current injection caused a cycle frequency increase in both types of bursting neuron.
source: Consistent also with the voltage-dependence of an endogenous pacemaker mechanism, membrane potential depolarization with current injection caused a cycle frequency increase in both types of bursting neuron, with the rates of plateauing and oscillatory bursting increasing as a function of injected current intensity (Figure 3B,C).
evidence: This is a finding from experimental data shown in Figure 3B,C.

claim: The I-V relationships of the two pacemaker phenotypes were statistically different (t-test; p<0.001) in the range of more depolarized membrane potential levels between −20 mV and 0 mV.
source: It is also noteworthy, however, that the I-V relationships of the two pacemaker phenotypes were statistically different (t-test; p<0.001) in the range of more depolarized membrane potential levels between −20 mV and 0 mV, thus indicating differences in properties that govern their membrane excitability.
evidence: This is a statistical analysis of experimental data with interpretation.

claim: No difference (t-test, p= 0.7) was found in the membrane input resistance measured around resting potential for plateau-like (1756 ± 667 MΩ) and burst-like pacemaker neurons (1574 ± 973 MΩ).
source: No difference (t-test, p= 0.7) was found in the membrane input resistance measured around resting potential for plateau-like (1756 ± 667 MΩ) and burst-like pacemaker neurons (1574 ± 973 MΩ).
evidence: This is a statistical analysis of experimental measurements.

claim: Out of the 10 embryonic preBötC neurons identified as plateauing pacemakers, the bursting activity of 8 was completely blocked in the presence of 50 µM FFA applied either alone (n = 4) or in co-application with 10 µM Ril (n = 4).
source: Out of the 10 embryonic preBötC neurons identified as plateauing pacemakers, the bursting activity of 8 of these was completely blocked in the presence of 50 µM FFA applied either alone (n = 4; Figure 4A, right panel) or in co-application with 10 µM Ril, which by itself was ineffective in blocking bursting activity (n = 4, Figure 4A, left panel).
evidence: This is a finding from pharmacological experiments shown in Figure 4A.

claim: For the remaining two plateauing cells, bursting activity was blocked in the presence of Ril alone (n = 2).
source: For the remaining two plateauing cells, bursting activity was blocked in the presence of Ril alone (n = 2).
evidence: This is a finding from pharmacological experiments.

claim: Pacemaker activity of the plateauing inspiratory neurons relies on a combination of both INaP and ICAN, with a predominant role played by ICAN.
source: These findings therefore suggest that pacemaker activity of the plateauing inspiratory neurons relies on a combination of both INaP and ICAN, with a predominant role played by the latter.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the pharmacological data.

claim: For the vast majority (13/17) of the oscillatory bursting neurons tested, pacemaker activity was blocked in the presence of 10 µM Ril alone (n = 8) or when co-applied with FFA (n = 5).
source: For the vast majority (13/17) of the oscillatory bursting neurons tested, pacemaker activity was blocked in the presence of 10 µM Ril alone (n = 8; data not shown) or when co-applied with FFA (n = 5; Figure 4B).
evidence: This is a finding from pharmacological experiments, with some data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: In the remaining four oscillatory bursting neurons, bursting was blocked by 50 µM FFA alone.
source: In the remaining four neurons, bursting was blocked by 50 µM FFA alone.
evidence: This is a finding from pharmacological experiments.

claim: For pacemaker neurons exhibiting a mixed DP pattern (n = 10), bursting activity was differentially sensitive to FFA and Ril, with plateau-like bursts being suppressed by FFA while short-lasting oscillatory bursts were blocked by Ril.
source: For pacemaker neurons exhibiting a mixed DP pattern (n = 10), bursting activity was differentially sensitive to FFA and Ril, with plateau-like bursts being suppressed by FFA while short-lasting oscillatory bursts were blocked by Ril (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is a finding from pharmacological experiments shown in Figure 4C.

claim: The heterogeneous patterns of discharge in pacemaker neurons of the embryonic preBötC network are associated with different combinations of membrane conductances: ICAN plays a major role for plateau pacemakers, INaP predominates in oscillatory pacemakers, whereas the relative conductance contribution in the mixed pacemaker phenotype is intermediate between these two.
source: Thus, the heterogeneous patterns of discharge in pacemaker neurons of the embryonic preBötC network within the period from E16.5 to E18.5 appear to be associated with different combinations of membrane conductances contributing to underlying drive potential activity: ICAN plays a major role for plateau pacemakers, INaP predominates in oscillatory pacemakers, whereas the relative conductance contribution in the mixed pacemaker phenotype is intermediate between these two.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the pharmacological data.

claim: Plateau and oscillatory pacemakers were found to be almost equally present at E16.5.
source: Plateau and oscillatory pacemakers were found to be almost equally present at E16.5, whereas oscillatory bursters were predominant (65.7%, n = 23/35) at E18.5 (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is a finding from developmental comparison shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Oscillatory bursters were predominant (65.7%, n = 23/35) at E18.5.
source: Plateau and oscillatory pacemakers were found to be almost equally present at E16.5, whereas oscillatory bursters were predominant (65.7%, n = 23/35) at E18.5 (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is a finding from developmental comparison shown in Figure 5A.

claim: At E18.5, the activity of only 8% (n = 3/35) of neurons was exclusively plateau-like.
source: At this later stage furthermore, the activity of only 8% (n = 3/35) of neurons was exclusively plateau-like, with the remaining 25.5% (n = 9/35) of cells expressing a mixed oscillatory/plateauing phenotype.
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from developmental comparison.

claim: At E18.5, 25.5% (n = 9/35) of cells expressed a mixed oscillatory/plateauing phenotype.
source: At this later stage furthermore, the activity of only 8% (n = 3/35) of neurons was exclusively plateau-like, with the remaining 25.5% (n = 9/35) of cells expressing a mixed oscillatory/plateauing phenotype.
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from developmental comparison.

claim: The proportions of the different pacemaker cell types were significantly different between E16.5 and E18.5 (chi-square test, p<0.001).
source: These proportions of the different pacemaker cell types were significantly different between the two embryonic stages (chi-square test, p<0.001).
evidence: This is a statistical analysis of developmental comparison data.

claim: Of 32 pacemaker neurons identified at E16.5, 19 were sensitive to Ril exposure.
source: Of 32 pacemaker neurons identified at E16.5, 19 were sensitive to Ril exposure (Figure 5C, left histogram) indicating that the preBötC pacemaker population contains significant proportions (ratio 60:40) of both INaP and presumed ICAN at this earlier embryonic age.
evidence: This is a finding from calcium imaging experiments shown in Figure 5C.

claim: The preBötC pacemaker population at E16.5 contains significant proportions (ratio 60:40) of both INaP and presumed ICAN.
source: Of 32 pacemaker neurons identified at E16.5, 19 were sensitive to Ril exposure (Figure 5C, left histogram) indicating that the preBötC pacemaker population contains significant proportions (ratio 60:40) of both INaP and presumed ICAN at this earlier embryonic age.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the riluzole sensitivity data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: At E18.5, pacemaker neurons were found to be predominantly sensitive to Ril (22/27 neurons).
source: In contrast, at E18.5, pacemaker neurons were found to be predominantly sensitive to Ril (22/27 neurons; Figure 5C, right), indicating that INaP is now the effective rhythmogenic mechanism in the majority of the pacemaker population at this older stage.
evidence: This is a finding from calcium imaging experiments shown in Figure 5C.

claim: INaP is the effective rhythmogenic mechanism in the majority of the pacemaker population at E18.5.
source: In contrast, at E18.5, pacemaker neurons were found to be predominantly sensitive to Ril (22/27 neurons; Figure 5C, right), indicating that INaP is now the effective rhythmogenic mechanism in the majority of the pacemaker population at this older stage.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the riluzole sensitivity data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: At E16.5 both types of pacemakers (riluzole sensitive INaP-dependent and riluzole-insensitive ICAN-dependent) are present in comparable proportions, while at E18.5, the same preBötC cell subset is mainly comprised of INaP-dependent pacemaker neurons.
source: Therefore, altogether these data support the conclusion that at E16.5 both types of pacemakers (riluzole sensitive INaP-dependent and riluzole-insensitive ICAN-dependent) are present in comparable proportions, while 2 days later in prenatal development, the same preBötC cell subset is mainly comprised of INaP-dependent pacemaker neurons.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the developmental comparison data.

claim: With gCAN at 2.5 nS, the model neuron produced repetitive, long-duration oscillations and burst discharge events that strongly resembled the plateau-like rhythmic activity recorded from biological pacemaker neurons.
source: With gCAN at 2.5 nS, the model neuron produced repetitive, long-duration oscillations and burst discharge events (Figure 6B) that strongly resembled the plateau-like rhythmic activity recorded from biological pacemaker neurons (c.f., Figure 2A).
evidence: This is a finding from computational modeling shown in Figure 6B compared to experimental data in Figure 2A.

claim: When gCAN was reduced to 0 nS, higher frequency short-lasting bursts were produced that were strikingly similar to the oscillatory pacemaker phenotype observed in vitro.
source: In contrast, when gCAN was reduced to 0 nS, higher frequency short-lasting bursts were now produced (Figure 6D) in a manner that was strikingly similar to the oscillatory pacemaker phenotype observed in vitro (c.f., Figure 2B).
evidence: This is a finding from computational modeling shown in Figure 6D compared to experimental data in Figure 2B.

claim: A hybrid model activity pattern that closely resembled the mixed biological pacemaker phenotype was observed when gCAN was set at an intermediate conductance value of 1 nS.
source: On the other hand, a hybrid model activity pattern (Figure 6C) that closely resembled the mixed biological pacemaker phenotype (c.f., Figure 2C) was observed when gCAN was set at an intermediate conductance value of 1 nS.
evidence: This is a finding from computational modeling shown in Figure 6C compared to experimental data in Figure 2C.

claim: As the proportion of artificial INaP conductance relative to gCAN was increased, the model pacemaker neuron switched from inactive to plateauing states, then transcended a mixed plateau/oscillatory state until eventually the transition to a regularized oscillatory bursting condition occurred.
source: Here again, as the proportion of artificial INaP conductance relative to gCAN was increased, the model pacemaker neuron switched from inactive to plateauing states, then transcended a mixed plateau/oscillatory state until eventually the transition to a regularized oscillatory bursting condition occurred (Figure 6E).
evidence: This is a finding from computational modeling shown in Figure 6E.

claim: Differences in proportion of the two conductances INaP and ICAN could underlie the different discharge patterns expressed by actual preBötC pacemaker neurons.
source: These in silico findings thus support the possibility that differences in proportion of the two conductances INaP and ICAN could underlie the different discharge patterns expressed by actual preBötC pacemaker neurons.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the computational modeling results.

claim: The developmental process responsible for the difference in functional composition of the inspiratory pacemaker population at E16.5 and E18.5 could involve a switch in the proportion of INaP and ICAN within individual neurons.
source: Additionally, they suggests that the developmental process responsible for the difference in functional composition of the inspiratory pacemaker population at E16.5 and E18.5 could involve a switch in this proportion, and thereby resultant rhythmic burst patterning, within individual neurons.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation based on the computational modeling results.

claim: At E16.5, application of 50 µM FFA significantly decreased the frequency of the ongoing spontaneous inspiratory rhythm by 46 ± 9% (t-test, p= 0.006).
source: At E16.5, application of 50 µM FFA (Figure 7A, left panel) or 20 µM Ril (Figure 7A, right panel) significantly decreased the frequency of the ongoing spontaneous inspiratory rhythm by 46 ± 9% (t-test, p= 0.006) and 89.7 ± 5% (Mann-Whitney test, p<0.001), respectively (Figure 7B, left histogram bars).
evidence: This is a finding from pharmacological experiments on network activity shown in Figure 7A,B.

claim: At E16.5, application of 20 µM Ril significantly decreased the frequency of the ongoing spontaneous inspiratory rhythm by 89.7 ± 5% (Mann-Whitney test, p<0.001).
source: At E16.5, application of 50 µM FFA (Figure 7A, left panel) or 20 µM Ril (Figure 7A, right panel) significantly decreased the frequency of the ongoing spontaneous inspiratory rhythm by 46 ± 9% (t-test, p= 0.006) and 89.7 ± 5% (Mann-Whitney test, p<0.001), respectively (Figure 7B, left histogram bars).
evidence: This is a finding from pharmacological experiments on network activity shown in Figure 7A,B.

claim: At E18.5, FFA and Ril treatments had no significant effect (t-test, p= 0.1 and 0.4 for FFA and Ril treatments, respectively), with the frequencies of the ongoing preBötC rhythms remaining unchanged.
source: Unexpectedly, however, the same drug treatments performed at E18.5 had no significant effect (t-test, p= 0.1 and 0.4 for FFA and Ril treatments, respectively), with the frequencies of the ongoing preBötC rhythms in each case remaining unchanged under either FFA (Figure 7C, left middle trace) or Ril (Figure 7C, right middle trace) application (Figure 7D, left bars).
evidence: This is a finding from pharmacological experiments on network activity shown in Figure 7C,D.

claim: When FFA and Ril were applied concomitantly, rhythmic preBötC activity was fully blocked at E16.5 (Mann-Whitney test, p<0.001).
source: Furthermore, when the drugs were applied concomitantly, rhythmic preBötC activity was fully blocked at E16.5 (Figure 7A, lower traces; 7B, right histogram bars; Mann-Whitney test, p<0.001), but rhythmic activity persisted at E18.5 (Figure 7C, lower traces) albeit at a significantly reduced cycle frequency (Figure 7D, right bars; Mann-Whitney test, p<0.01).
evidence: This is a finding from pharmacological experiments on network activity shown in Figure 7A,B.

claim: When FFA and Ril were applied concomitantly at E18.5, rhythmic activity persisted albeit at a significantly reduced cycle frequency (Mann-Whitney test, p<0.01).
source: Furthermore, when the drugs were applied concomitantly, rhythmic preBötC activity was fully blocked at E16.5 (Figure 7A, lower traces; 7B, right histogram bars; Mann-Whitney test, p<0.001), but rhythmic activity persisted at E18.5 (Figure 7C, lower traces) albeit at a significantly reduced cycle frequency (Figure 7D, right bars; Mann-Whitney test, p<0.01).
evidence: This is a finding from pharmacological experiments on network activity shown in Figure 7C,D.

claim: At E16.5, inspiratory network rhythmogenesis requires co-activation of INaP and ICAN.
source: Altogether, these data therefore show that at E16.5, inspiratory network rhythmogenesis requires co-activation of INaP and ICAN, whereas later at E18.5, blockade of either conductance fails to fully prevent the generation of rhythmic activity.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the pharmacological experiments on network activity.

claim: At E18.5, blockade of either INaP or ICAN conductance fails to fully prevent the generation of rhythmic activity.
source: Altogether, these data therefore show that at E16.5, inspiratory network rhythmogenesis requires co-activation of INaP and ICAN, whereas later at E18.5, blockade of either conductance fails to fully prevent the generation of rhythmic activity.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the pharmacological experiments on network activity.

claim: A developmental change has occurred in the mechanistic basis for respiratory network rhythm generation, which is linked to a less predominant role played by endogenous pacemaker neurons at E18.5.
source: This in turn indicates that a developmental change has indeed occurred in the mechanistic basis for respiratory network rhythm generation, which evidently is linked to a less predominant role played by endogenous pacemaker neurons at the older embryonic stage.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the pharmacological data on network rhythmogenesis.

claim: The mean amplitude value of excitatory synaptic currents obtained for 17 neurons at E18.5 (55 ± 0.9 nA) was >3 fold greater than that measured in 14 cells at E16.5 (15 ± 0.9 nA) (Mann-Whitney test, p<0.001).
source: The synaptic current magnitudes obtained at E16.5 and E18.5 (red traces in lower Figure 8A and B, respectively) were found to be significantly different (Mann-Whitney test, p<0.001), with the mean amplitude value obtained for 17 neurons at E18.5 (55 ± 0.9 nA) being >3 fold greater than that measured in 14 cells at E16.5 (15 ± 0.9 nA), (Figure 8C).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from voltage clamp recordings shown in Figure 8.

claim: Excitatory post-synaptic currents increase developmentally, supporting the hypothesis that the embryonic inspiratory network operates through different age-dependent strategies.
source: The finding that excitatory post-synaptic currents do indeed appear to increase developmentally supports the hypothesis that the embryonic inspiratory network operates through different age-dependent strategies: one based principally on a subset of neuronal pacemakers and another in which overall circuit connectivity also plays a critical role.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the synaptic current data.

claim: Neurons with endogenous pacemaker properties are present in the mouse embryonic preBötzinger network, constituting a functionally heterogeneous subpopulation in terms of their burst discharge patterns and underlying burst-promoting conductances INaP and ICAN.
source: First, neurons with endogenous pacemaker properties are present in the mouse embryonic preBötzinger network, constituting a functionally heterogeneous subpopulation in terms of their burst discharge patterns and underlying burst-promoting conductances INaP- and ICAN.
evidence: This is a summary of the main findings from the study.

claim: The relative proportions of different pacemaker phenotypes change as prenatal development progresses.
source: Second, these different pacemaker phenotypes are not invariably represented within the embryonic network during the prenatal period, but their relative proportions change as prenatal development progresses.
evidence: This is a summary of the main findings from the study.

claim: The overall mechanism responsible for preBötC network rhythmogenesis changes during embryonic development, switching from a purely pacemaker neuron-driven, INaP/ICAN-dependent mechanism to an emergent network process in which both neuronal pacemakers and circuit excitatory synaptic connectivity play important roles.
source: Third, the overall mechanism responsible for preBötC network rhythmogenesis also changes during embryonic development, switching from a purely pacemaker neuron-driven, INaP/ICAN-dependent mechanism to an emergent network process in which both neuronal pacemakers and circuit excitatory synaptic connectivity appear to play important roles.
evidence: This is a summary of the main findings from the study.

claim: The establishment of pacemaker and synaptic mechanisms acting in cooperation serves to ensure that a fully effective respiratory motor command is available at the time of birth.
source: Presumably, the establishment of these two mechanisms acting in cooperation serves to ensure that a fully effective respiratory motor command is available at the time of birth.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the functional significance of the findings.

claim: Two major types of prenatal preBötC pacemaker neurons are present: one whose bursting activity depends mainly on INaP and another that is dominated by ICAN.
source: As also found in early postnatal rodents (Thoby-Brisson and Ramirez, 2001; Del Negro et al., 2002; Pena et al., 2004; Del Negro et al., 2005), two major types of prenatal preBötC pacemaker neurons are present: one whose bursting activity depends mainly on the activation of a Ril-sensitive, voltage-dependent persistent sodium current (INaP) and another that is dominated by a FFA-sensitive, Ca2+-activated nonspecific cationic current (ICAN).
evidence: This is a finding from the study compared to prior literature with citations.

claim: A proportion of pacemaker neurons express bursting activity that arises from both INaP and ICAN mechanisms, indicative of an intermediary pacemaker phenotype.
source: Furthermore, a proportion of pacemaker neurons express bursting activity that arises from both mechanisms, indicative of an intermediary pacemaker phenotype.
evidence: This is a finding from the study.

claim: In the embryonic network, ICAN is prevalent in generating long and slowly repeating plateau-like activity, while INaP tends to underlie shorter and more rapid burst discharge.
source: We also found that in the embryonic network, the two main pacemaker mechanisms produce a depolarizing potential drive with distinctly different durations and cycle frequencies - ICAN is prevalent in generating long and slowly repeating plateau-like activity, while INaP tends to underlie shorter and more rapid burst discharge - thus indicating that the pacemaker subtypes are distinguishable according to both the conductance mechanisms responsible for the initiation of their bursts as well as for burst termination.
evidence: This is a finding from the study.

claim: Plateau-like inspiratory pacemaker bursting is considerably more prevalent at earlier embryonic ages (representing ~50% of the total pacemaker population) but is then largely superseded by faster, short-duration oscillatory bursting as development progresses.
source: Additionally, we observed that plateau-like inspiratory pacemaker bursting is considerably more prevalent at earlier embryonic ages (representing ~50% of the total pacemaker population) but is then largely superseded by faster, short-duration oscillatory bursting as development progresses.
evidence: This is a finding from the developmental comparison in the study.

claim: The shape, duration and regularity of inspiratory pacemaker bursts occurring at E18.5 more closely resemble the discharge patterns expressed by preBötC pacemakers in the neonatal animal than those at E16.5.
source: Perhaps unsurprisingly, the shape, duration and regularity of inspiratory pacemaker bursts occurring at E18.5, and in contrast to the considerably slower, yet robust, plateauing activity expressed at E16.5, more closely resemble the discharge patterns expressed by preBötC pacemakers in the neonatal animal (cf., Pena et al., 2004; Del Negro et al., 2005).
evidence: This is a comparison of the study's findings to prior literature with citations.

claim: Together with developmental changes in the balance of membrane conductances engaged in initiating burst-driving potentials, the conductance mechanisms required for burst termination in the postnatal respiratory network are also being established and refined at late embryonic stages.
source: It is likely, therefore, that together with developmental changes in the balance of membrane conductances engaged in initiating burst-driving potentials (see below), the conductance mechanisms required for their appropriate cycle-by-cycle termination in the postnatal respiratory network are also being established and refined at late embryonic stages.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the findings.

claim: Cadmium-sensitive (therefore presumed ICAN-dependent) pacemaker neurons are more readily detected in the preBötC network of juvenile mice (P8 - P10) than at neonatal (P0 – P5) stages.
source: Significantly, previous studies have reported that cadmium-sensitive (therefore presumed ICAN-dependent) pacemaker neurons are more readily detected in the preBötC network of juvenile mice (P8 - P10) than at neonatal (P0 – P5) stages (Pena et al., 2004) where they were found to represent < 1% of recorded inspiratory cells compared to 7.5% in the older animals (Del Negro et al., 2005).
evidence: This is information from prior literature with citations.

claim: ICAN-dependent pacemaker neurons represent < 1% of recorded inspiratory cells at neonatal stages compared to 7.5% in juvenile animals.
source: Significantly, previous studies have reported that cadmium-sensitive (therefore presumed ICAN-dependent) pacemaker neurons are more readily detected in the preBötC network of juvenile mice (P8 - P10) than at neonatal (P0 – P5) stages (Pena et al., 2004) where they were found to represent < 1% of recorded inspiratory cells compared to 7.5% in the older animals (Del Negro et al., 2005).
evidence: This is information from prior literature with citations.

claim: Prior observations are consistent with the finding that in a developmental period around the time of birth embryonic ICAN-dependent inspiratory pacemakers are much less prevalent than INaP-dependent ones.
source: These observations are therefore consistent with our own finding that in a developmental period around the time of birth embryonic ICAN-dependent inspiratory pacemakers are much less prevalent than INaP-dependent ones.
evidence: This is an interpretation comparing the study's findings to prior literature.

claim: The functional significance of the re-emergence of the ICAN-dependent pacemaker subtype during the second post-natal week remains unknown.
source: However, the functional significance of the re-emergence of the ICAN-dependent pacemaker subtype during the second post-natal week (Pena et al., 2004; Del Negro et al., 2005) remains unknown.
evidence: This identifies a knowledge gap in the literature with citations.

claim: The finding that a small group of recorded pacemaker cells could express a mixture of both plateau- and oscillatory-based discharge patterns was indicative of a mechanistic switch that was transitioning within individual neurons.
source: Although such processes are not mutually exclusive, the finding that a small group of our in vitro recorded pacemaker cells could express a mixture of both plateau- and oscillatory-based discharge patterns, as similarly produced by our model neuron with intermediate gNaP and gCAN proportions (see also Dunmyre et al., 2011), was indicative of a mechanistic switch that was transitioning within individual neurons.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental and modeling data with a citation.

claim: Pharmacological attenuation of ICAN and INaP at E16.5 completely blocked rhythmic preBötC network activity.
source: First, pharmacological attenuation of ICAN and INaP at E16.5 completely blocked rhythmic preBötC network activity, whereas the same treatment of slices at E18.5 reduced, but failed to completely suppress ongoing network activity.
evidence: This is a finding from pharmacological experiments on network activity.

claim: The same pharmacological treatment at E18.5 reduced, but failed to completely suppress ongoing network activity.
source: First, pharmacological attenuation of ICAN and INaP at E16.5 completely blocked rhythmic preBötC network activity, whereas the same treatment of slices at E18.5 reduced, but failed to completely suppress ongoing network activity.
evidence: This is a finding from pharmacological experiments on network activity.

claim: A fundamental developmental change had occurred whereby network rhythmogenesis has shifted from an obligatory pacemaker-driven mechanism to one in which pacemaker neurons were no longer uniquely essential.
source: Notwithstanding the fact that the vast majority of inspiratory network neurons, including pacemakers and non-pacemakers alike, possess both NaP and CAN conductances (Del Negro et al., 2011) and are therefore affected by our drug treatments, these findings indicate that a fundamental developmental change had occurred whereby network rhythmogenesis has shifted from an obligatory pacemaker-driven mechanism to one in which pacemaker neurons were no longer uniquely essential.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the pharmacological data with a citation.

claim: The strength of excitatory glutamatergic synaptic transmission is significantly stronger throughout the preBötC circuitry of E18.5 compared to E16.5 slices.
source: Second, as shown by in vitro experimental data, the strength of excitatory glutamatergic synaptic transmission is significantly stronger throughout the preBötC circuitry of E18.5 compared to E16.5 slices.
evidence: This is a finding from voltage clamp experiments.

claim: At earlier embryonic stages, pacemaker neurons play an essential role in network rhythm generation but later in the prenatal period, the contribution of glutamatergic synaptic interactions becomes increasingly important so that nearer the time of birth, both cellular pacemaker properties and synaptic excitation are critical to network rhythmogenesis.
source: On this basis, therefore, we propose that at earlier embryonic stages, pacemaker neurons play an essential role in network rhythm generation but that later in the prenatal period, the contribution of glutamatergic synaptic interactions becomes increasingly important so that nearer the time of birth, both cellular pacemaker properties and synaptic excitation are critical to network rhythmogenesis.
evidence: This is a proposed model based on the combined experimental findings.

claim: The developmental plasticity occurring in the late embryo embodies essential features of both the 'pacemaker neuron' and 'group-pacemaker' hypotheses that have been proposed to account for respiratory rhythm generation in the early postnatal rodent.
source: Interestingly, such a developmental plasticity occurring in the late embryo embodies essential features of both the 'pacemaker neuron' (Pena et al., 2004; Ramirez et al., 2011) and 'group-pacemaker' hypotheses (Rekling and Feldman, 1998; Pena et al., 2004; Feldman and Del Negro, 2006) that have been proposed to account for respiratory rhythm generation in the early postnatal rodent (for review, see Feldman et al., 2013).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the findings in the context of prior hypotheses with citations.

claim: The composition of the pacemaker population, both in terms of pacemaker subtypes and their implication in overall network rhythmogenesis undergo significant maturational changes during the prenatal period.
source: In conclusion, the present study provides the first description of a heterogeneous population of neurons bestowed with pacemaker properties in the embryonic respiratory network. The composition of this population, both in terms of pacemaker subtypes and their implication in overall network rhythmogenesis undergo significant maturational changes during the prenatal period.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion from the study's findings.

claim: The pacemaker cell subpopulation is exclusively responsible for network rhythmogenesis at earlier embryonic stages, but then assumes a cooperative role with recurrent synaptic excitation throughout the wider network immediately prior to birth.
source: However, our in vitro results from differential pharmacology lead to the conclusion that the pacemaker cell subpopulation is exclusively responsible for network rhythmogenesis at earlier embryonic stages, but then assumes a cooperative role with recurrent synaptic excitation throughout the wider network immediately prior to birth.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the pharmacological experiments.

claim: A better understanding of prenatal developmental processes could provide relevant insights into clinical aspects of early post-natal respiratory disorders.
source: A better understanding of such prenatal developmental processes could in turn provide relevant insights into clinical aspects of early post-natal respiratory disorders.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about potential clinical relevance.

claim: Brainstem transverse slice preparations that isolated the preBötC network were obtained from mouse embryos at embryonic day (E) 16.5 or E18.5.
source: Brainstem transverse slice preparations that isolated the preBötC network were obtained from mouse embryos using the following procedures: pregnant mice were killed by cervical dislocation on embryonic day (E) 16.5 or E18.5, the day of the plug being considered as E0.5.
evidence: This describes the experimental methodology used in the study.

claim: A 450-µm-thick slice, with its anterior limit set 250–300 µm caudal to the more caudal extension of the facial nucleus, was isolated.
source: A 450-µm-thick slice, with its anterior limit set 250–300 µm caudal to the more caudal extension of the facial nucleus, was isolated.
evidence: This describes the experimental methodology used in the study.

claim: Such slice preparations encompass the region containing a significant portion of the preBötC network capable of spontaneously generating fictive rhythmic inspiratory activity.
source: Such slice preparations encompass the region containing a significant portion of the preBötC network capable of spontaneously generating fictive rhythmic inspiratory activity (Thoby-Brisson et al., 2005; Toporikova et al., 2015) are devoid of the more rostral Bötzinger complex and contain only the most rostral region of the more caudal rVRG.
evidence: This describes the experimental preparation with citations to prior work.

claim: All neuronal populations examined were considered to be integral components of the preBötzinger network.
source: On this basis, therefore, all neuronal populations examined were considered to be integral components of the preBötzinger network.
evidence: This is an assumption about the anatomical identity of recorded neurons.

claim: Neurons were classified as pacemakers if they remained rhythmically active during exposure to a cocktail of agents known to block chemical synaptic transmission in the preBötC network.
source: Accordingly, neurons expressing fluorescence fluctuations in time with fictive inspiration in control conditions were classified as pacemakers if they remained rhythmically active during subsequent exposure to a cocktail of agents known to block chemical synaptic transmission in the preBötC network (see Material and methods).
evidence: This describes the operational definition and methodology for identifying pacemaker neurons.

claim: Under conditions of synaptic blockade, network electrical activity ceased as did rhythmic fluorescent changes in most of the previously identified inspiratory neurons.
source: Under such conditions of synaptic blockade, network electrical activity ceased as did rhythmic fluorescent changes in most of the previously identified inspiratory neurons (Figure 1C, black traces).
evidence: This is a finding from calcium imaging experiments shown in Figure 1C.

claim: A small proportion of monitored cells continued to express spontaneous fluorescence fluctuations at unrelated frequencies during synaptic blockade.
source: However, a small proportion of monitored cells continued to express spontaneous fluorescence fluctuations at unrelated frequencies (Figure 1C, red traces).
evidence: This is a finding from calcium imaging experiments shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Riluzole is a blocker of INaP.
source: We therefore bath-applied Riluzole (Ril; 10 µM) a blocker of INaP (Urbani and Belluzzi, 2000), and Flufenamic Acid (FFA; 50 µM) a blocker of ICAN (Guinamard et al., 2004) onto synaptically-isolated, patch-clamp recorded neurons.
evidence: This is established pharmacological knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: Flufenamic Acid is a blocker of ICAN.
source: We therefore bath-applied Riluzole (Ril; 10 µM) a blocker of INaP (Urbani and Belluzzi, 2000), and Flufenamic Acid (FFA; 50 µM) a blocker of ICAN (Guinamard et al., 2004) onto synaptically-isolated, patch-clamp recorded neurons.
evidence: This is established pharmacological knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: The vast majority of inspiratory network neurons, including pacemakers and non-pacemakers alike, possess both NaP and CAN conductances.
source: Notwithstanding the fact that the vast majority of inspiratory network neurons, including pacemakers and non-pacemakers alike, possess both NaP and CAN conductances (Del Negro et al., 2011) and are therefore affected by our drug treatments, these findings indicate that a fundamental developmental change had occurred whereby network rhythmogenesis has shifted from an obligatory pacemaker-driven mechanism to one in which pacemaker neurons were no longer uniquely essential.
evidence: This is established knowledge from prior literature with a citation.
